fullPassage:
(A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

(B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

(C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders ①<u>who</u> were reading below grade level. The goal was to ②<u>raise</u> the reading level of the students. Emma was in one of Sandy's groups, and she was not ③<u>improving</u>. She lacked patience and often lost ④<u>focusing</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①who(관계대명사), ②raise(동사원형), ③improving(진행형)은 정상입니다. ④focusing은 lost의 목적어이므로 명사 focus가 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① who: 관계대명사 (graders who)
✅ ② raise: to raise(to부정사)
✅ ③ improving: was not improving
❌ ④ focusing → focus: lost focus(명사 목적어)
det.tip: lost focus(집중력을 잃다): focus는 명사. focusing은 동명사/현재분사

questions.passage: That evening after school, Sandy reflected on ①<u>what</u> Emma had said. Sandy recalled research ②<u>suggested</u> she needed to increase the number of words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction ③<u>in addition to</u> the small-group time. Sandy let Emma ④<u>select</u> a book from a handful of books.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①what(관계대명사), ③in addition to(전치사구), ④select(동사원형)는 정상입니다. ②suggested는 research를 수식하는 현재분사이므로 suggesting이 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① what: 관계대명사 what (선행사 포함)
❌ ② suggested → suggesting: 현재분사 (research suggesting)
✅ ③ in addition to: ~에 추가하여
✅ ④ select: let + O + V(원형)
det.tip: research suggesting(연구가 제안하는): 현재분사로 research를 수식

questions.passage: They would continue to ①<u>swap</u> back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level as Emma's ability ②<u>to sound</u> out words improved. Sandy noticed that Emma started to make it through the entire lesson without ③<u>become</u> disruptive. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her ④<u>want</u> to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①swap(동사원형), ②to sound(to부정사), ④want(동사원형)는 정상입니다. ③become은 without 뒤에 동명사가 필요하므로 becoming이 올바릅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① swap: continue to V
✅ ② to sound: ability to V
❌ ③ become → becoming: without + -ing
✅ ④ want: made her want (사역동사 + O + V원형)
det.tip: without + -ing: 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사. becoming(O), become(X)

questions.passage: Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. Every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. Emma was in one of Sandy's groups and was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became ①<u>disruptive</u>. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to ②<u>increase</u> the number of words Emma was reading. Sandy let Emma ③<u>select</u> a book. Over time, they saw improvement. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to ④<u>refuse</u> to read other books!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④refuse(거부하다)는 원문의 try(시도하다)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ refuse(거부) → try(시도): 자신감이 생겨 읽기를 '시도'하려는 맥락
det.tip: try(시도) ↔ refuse(거부): 자신감으로 인한 적극적 태도 변화

questions.passage: That evening after school, Sandy ①<u>reflected</u> on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to ②<u>increase</u> the number of words Emma was reading. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in ③<u>addition</u> to the small-group time. In those meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a ④<u>large collection</u> of books that were at her reading level.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어(구) 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②③은 원문과 일치합니다. ④large collection(대규모 소장)은 원문의 handful(소수)을 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ large collection → handful: 소수의 책에서 골랐음
det.tip: a handful of(소수의) ↔ a large collection(대규모): 규모 변조

questions.passage: They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but ①<u>surely</u>, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling ②<u>anxious</u>. More than anything, her newfound ③<u>doubt</u> made her want to try and read ④<u>other</u> books!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①②④는 원문과 일치합니다. ③doubt(의심)은 원문의 confidence(자신감)를 반의어로 교체한 것입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①②④: 원문 그대로
✅ ③ doubt(의심) → confidence(자신감): '의심'이 아닌 '자신감'이 다른 책을 읽고 싶게 만듦
det.tip: confidence(자신감) ↔ doubt(의심): 긍정적 변화의 핵심 동력
